faq.q: Is this an AI grammar checker?
faq.a: No — it's rule-based, not AI, and says so. It applies fixed patterns to catch high-confidence mistakes: double spaces, spacing around punctuation, repeated words, could/would/should 'of', common misspellings, a/an before vowels, filler words and possible passive voice. It can't judge meaning-dependent choices like affect vs effect, so review each suggestion before applying it.

faq.q: What scores does it show after a check?
faq.a: It displays word count, the number of active issues, a Flesch–Kincaid readability score (0–100), and a Writing Score out of 100. The Writing Score starts at 100 and drops based on the ratio of issues to words, with extra penalties when readability is low. Issues are also grouped by type (spelling, grammar, style, punctuation, spacing, capitalization) with colour-coded counts.

faq.q: Does it understand Indian English like 'revert back' or 'cousin brother'?
faq.a: It has specific Indian-English rules. It flags genuine redundancies — 'revert back', 'return back', 'discuss about', 'reason is because' — and suggests 'cousin' for 'cousin brother/sister' and 'good at' instead of 'good in'. The tool's own notes point out that lakh, crore and prepone are standard Indian English and shouldn't be treated as errors.

faq.q: Can I apply fixes automatically, and is my text saved?
faq.a: Where a correction exists, each issue has an 'Apply fix' button that replaces the text in place and re-scans (since positions shift), plus an 'Ignore' button. You can copy the corrected text or download it as corrected.txt. Your draft autosaves to local storage under grammarCheckerText, and recent checks are kept under gc_hist so you can watch issue counts fall across revisions.
